thread:
maria.g: FYI customer reported a 400 when calling /v1/embeddings. They say dimensions don't match their model (expect 1536) but our error is kinda vague. billing spike too. any quick ideas?

alex.t: Can you paste the request body they sent? usually shape issues are client wrapping single string as nested list.

maria.g: Pasted below (redacted):
```json
{"model":"text-embedding-ada-002","input":[["How to scale inference"]]}
```
Customer says they used a helper that auto-batches and sometimes wraps single inputs.

sasha: aha classic. If the model expects a single string or an array of strings like `["a","b"]`, but you pass `[["a"]]`, server will treat the outer as batch and the inner as a list item — it can change how we validate shape or even try to embed arrays as vectors if double-encoded. Does the API return dimension info?

maria.g: This is the error they got from our endpoint: `400 Bad Request: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768` and the response body had minimal context. They attached a full curl and logs.

alex.t: That error usually means they invoked a different model or our runtime inferred the wrong target. Two immediate checks: 1) confirm the `model` param actually maps to a 1536-dim embedding model (customer may have switched from open-source 768-dim model) 2) confirm the `input` is flattened.

maria.g: I asked for the full request. Customer sent this curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":[["How to scale inference"]]}'
```
They said their JS SDK wraps single inputs as arrays, so they sometimes pass nested arrays.

sasha: Root cause highly likely: double-wrapped input -> server tries to treat the inner array as precomputed vector or a multi-part item and validation ends up ambiguous. We should reproduce. Can someone spin a quick repro in curl/python?

alex.t: Reproduced locally. Two variants: correct and incorrect.

Incorrect (double-wrapped)
```json
{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":[["foo bar"]]}
```
Response: 400 + message: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768"

Correct
```json
{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["foo bar"]}
```
Response: 200 + embeddings: array of 1536 floats

maria.g: Any guess why wrong one returns 768 specifically?

alex.t: Common pattern: when we see nested arrays we attempt to detect if the inner array is already an embedding vector (numbers) vs text. In a buggy branch we interpreted the inner array as a tokenized/embed-like structure and then ended up mapping to a smaller model profile. But the product impact is: customer sees inscrutable 400 and gets billed for the request throughput because the request hit the runtime before validation stopped metering.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026 — support escalation: embeddings dimension mismatch caused by nested array input. Assigned to eng-runtime.

sasha: For immediate customer unblock suggest two options: 1) Ask them to flatten inputs (quick fix). Provide code snippet to sanitize. 2) If they can't change client quickly, we can add a request-side pre-validation rule that rejects nested string arrays with a clearer message.

alex.t: Sent a small repro script and a recommended fix to customer: sanitize like `if(Array.isArray(input) && input.length === 1 && Array.isArray(input[0])) input = input[0];` for JS. Also note Content-Type must be `application/json` — we saw one customer send `text/plain` which further confused parsing.

maria.g: Customer applied the JS fix and confirmed embeddings returned correctly. They also reported a billing spike — they saw ~1000 failed calls in a minute. Can we explain billing?

alex.t: Those failed calls reached the runtime and consumed compute (batch slot) before our schema validator rejected them. For now we can offer a partial credit and advise eng-runtime to early-fail before heavy batching. I'll file PR.

sasha: Filed PR #4281 to add early validation for nested string arrays + clearer error message: `400 Bad Request: expected input to be string or array of strings. Received nested arrays; try flattening single-item arrays`. Also added telemetry to track this error rate.

maria.g: Awesome. Customer asked for repro snippet to share with their devs. Dropping both the bad and good curl + python examples.

alex.t: Python quick example to show correct vs incorrect:
```python
import requests
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings"
headers = {"Authorization":"Bearer $TOKEN","Content-Type":"application/json"}
# incorrect (double-wrapped)
bad = {"model":"open-embed-1536","input":[["How to scale inference"]]}
# correct
good = {"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["How to scale inference"]]} 
print(requests.post(url,json=bad,headers=headers).status_code)
print(requests.post(url,json=good,headers=headers).status_code)
```

maria.g: Customer validated, everything green. Leaving thread open until PR merges and we confirm refund decision. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: PR #4281 merged into main by sasha.

sasha: Follow-up: eng-runtime will add a metric to monitor `nested_array_input_errors`. We'll keep an eye and consider a library change to SDKs to avoid the pattern.

maria.g: I'll email the billing team for a discretionary credit for the spike (support ticket attached). Closing once billing confirms.

customer-jen: Thanks so much for the quick help team — fixed on our side and appreciate the credit check. :pray:
